subject: Packaging: transient downgrade window, bundle credits, and SLA scenarios
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging question — transient downgrade windows, credits, and SLA impact

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week — appreciate the walkthrough on Dedicated vs Reserved throughput. A few follow-ups from procurement as we're lining up the contract:

- Transient downgrade window: we need clarity on how long Clearline would have to step down from a higher-tier/throughput bundle to a smaller one without penalty. Is that a fixed 30/60/90-day window, or can it be staged?
- Credits: if we step down mid-quarter, how are credits applied for unused capacity (seat/burst/throughput)? Are credits pro-rated or converted to account credits? Do credits expire?
- Feature bundling: our security team expects certain features (longer retention on logs, audit export) to remain available even if we step down — will those be preserved or gated by tier?
- Quantization/latency: procurement asked whether applying aggressive quantization (8-bit / q4) to meet cost targets has any SLA/latency ramifications that would affect our p99 SLOs.

If you can send two simple scenarios (a 60-day and a 90-day transient downgrade) with the credit math and the SLA impact callouts, that would let procurement and engineering decide quickly. We're also evaluating a 3-month pilot and could consider a temporary concession if the economics line up.

Attached: Clearline_MAL_v1.pdf (redacted) — shows our preferred terms.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Liu
Dir., Procurement
Clearline Health

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — transient downgrade windows, credits, and SLA impact

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together two pragmatic options below and attached a stepdown matrix (proposed_stepdown_matrix.xlsx). High-level: we can support staged downgrade windows, but we recommend a single defined protection period to keep billing and capacity planning simple.

Option A — 60-day transient downgrade window (recommended):
- Downgrade allowed once per 12-month period; must notify 7 days before effective date.
- Unused throughput/seat credits: pro-rated and issued as account credit within 14 days; credits expire after 12 months.
- Critical security/features (audit export, extended retention for logs up to 90 days): preserved for 60 days after downgrade; beyond that they will move to default retention on the lower tier unless converted to a paid add-on.
- Quantization guidance: conservative quantization (q8/q4_1) for batch inference shows negligible tail-impact for most workloads; aggressive q4 can add ~10–30ms to p99 depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate. We recommend testing with your p99 traces in a short pilot.

Option B — 90-day transient downgrade window (concession path):
- Same as above but 90 days protection.
- One-time onboarding credit: up to 25% of first quarter committed spend (subject to legal approval). Any concession >20% requires finance approval.
- Pilot discount: we can provide a 20% pilot discount for 3 months (applied after first invoice, credit line item).

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm target p99 latency and expected peak token throughput (RPS or tokens/sec) so we can quantify the latency delta with quantized variants?
2) If procurement is leaning to the 90-day path, we will route a concession request to finance (Ben/Finance) and prepare an updated MAL/DocuSign.

Attaching: proposed_stepdown_matrix.xlsx (contains credit math examples).

Happy to hop on a 20–30 min call tomorrow to walk through the examples.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 13:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Clearline concession guidance

Logan / Kim — quick internal note before we send a final to Sara:

- I'm OK with approving a 60-day transient downgrade window + pro-rated account credits expiring after 12 months as a standard offer.
- For the 90-day protection with a one-time onboarding credit up to 25%: finance sign-off is required for anything >20%. Recommend we offer 20% as the standard concession and leave room to escalate to 25% if legal/finance pushback is minimal.
- Pilot discount: 20% for 3 months is reasonable; flag that discounts must be applied as invoice credits (not below-list price) and reported in our commission system.

Also note: we should attach the latency note for quantization as a non-binding engineering advisory and require a short pilot (2 weeks) to measure p99 impact. If the pilot shows >15% p99 degradation, we include an auto-fallback clause to revert to the non-quantized variant.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — transient downgrade window, bundle credits, and SLA impact

Hi Sara — quick follow-up with a consolidated offer after internal review (see attached Clearline_Stepdown_Matrix_v2.xlsx):

Summary (concise):
- Standard: 60-day transient downgrade window (once per 12 months), unused capacity credited pro-rata to account credits, credits expire after 12 months. Critical features (audit export, extended log retention up to 90 days) preserved for the 60-day protection period.
- Concession (if you choose a 90-day protection window): we can extend protection to 90 days and provide a one-time onboarding credit of 20% of quarter 1 committed spend (finance pre-approved up to 20%). We can escalate to 25% with final Finance sign-off.
- Pilot: 20% pilot discount for the first 3 months (applied as invoice credits, not a change to list price).
- Quantization: recommended to run a controlled pilot. Aggressive quantization (q4) can increase p99 by ~10–30ms in some workflows; we will include an auto-fallback clause if pilot shows >15% p99 degradation.

Requested info from Clearline to finalize numbers:
- Target p99 SLO (ms) you expect us to meet for the pilot
- Expected peak tokens/sec and average sequence length (or a sanitized trace/sample)
- Whether you want the 60-day standard or the 90-day concession path (if 90-day, indicate if you want us to seek the additional 5% credit escalation)

If you confirm the 90-day path and we receive the token numbers, I will open a finance concession ticket and circulate a draft MAL + DocuSign link. Otherwise we'll prepare the standard 60-day amendment and the pilot MOU.

Links: Mutual Action Plan (internal view): https://redwood.app/ma/CL-2026-0917
DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/XYZ-CL-2026-0917

Attachments: Clearline_Stepdown_Matrix_v2.xlsx (updated credit examples and sample invoices)

Best,
Logan
Logan Wright
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
